name: Battle of Grunwald
note: The armies formed opposing lines along a northeast-southwest axis; the plan turns that axis across the page and shows no compass. The three villages are placed only as corners of the field, and the accounts do not say exactly where each lay. Later research put the main battlefield elsewhere than the traditional site. The Order's army is shown as two bodies, one under Wallenrode against the Lithuanians and one under Kuno von Lichtenstein; the accounts do not say how the rest stood. The accounts call the fight against Kuno's force one on the Polish right flank; it is drawn against the Polish centre, the part of the Polish troops nearest the Lithuanians. Jan Długosz described the Lithuanian retreat as a rout of their whole army and the Order as pursuing it; modern historians take it as a planned manoeuvre, and Stephen Turnbull doubts that it was a feigned retreat in the usual sense. The plan follows the Cronica conflictus, which has the Lithuanians returning. Where the Polish reserves, the Grand Master's banners and the Lithuanians stood when they came in is not stated; they are placed by judgement.

phases.title: The two armies form opposing lines
phases.text: The Polish-Lithuanian army stood with Polish heavy cavalry on its left, Lithuanian light cavalry on its right and mercenaries in the centre. The Order set its heavy cavalry against the Lithuanians and waited to be attacked.
phases.quote: The armies formed opposing lines along a northeast–southwest axis.

phases.title: Vytautas attacks the Order's left flank
phases.text: The Order had hoped the other side would attack first. Vytautas, supported by the Polish banners, went in against the Order's left flank, and the Lithuanian cavalry fought more than an hour.
phases.quote: Vytautas, supported by the Polish banners, started an assault on the left flank of the Teutonic forces.

phases.title: The Lithuanian light cavalry retreats
phases.text: After more than an hour of heavy fighting the Lithuanian light cavalry began a full retreat from the left flank of the Teutonic forces.
phases.quote: After more than an hour of heavy fighting, the Lithuanian light cavalry began a full retreat.

phases.title: Heavy fighting breaks out between Poles and the Order
phases.text: While the Lithuanians were retreating, Kuno von Lichtenstein's force fell on the Polish side. Six of Wallenrode's banners did not pursue the Lithuanians but joined the attack, and the royal banner of Kraków was lost and soon recaptured.
phases.quote: Six of von Walenrode's banners did not pursue the retreating Lithuanians, instead joining the attack on the right flank.

phases.title: The king deploys his second line
phases.text: Władysław II Jagiełło deployed his reserves, the second line of his army, against the Teutonic force that was pressing the Polish side.
phases.quote: Władysław II Jagiełło deployed his reserves — the second line of his army.

phases.title: The Grand Master's 16 banners and the last reserves
phases.text: Von Jungingen led 16 banners, almost a third of the original Teutonic strength, to the Polish side, and the king committed his third line. The fighting reached the Polish command.
phases.quote: The melee reached the Polish command

phases.title: The Lithuanians return and strike from behind
phases.text: The reorganised Lithuanians came back and attacked von Jungingen from the rear. The Order was by then outnumbered by the mass of Polish knights and the advancing Lithuanian cavalry.
phases.quote: At that time, the reorganised Lithuanians returned to the battle, attacking von Jungingen from the rear.

phases.title: Von Jungingen is killed
phases.text: Von Jungingen tried to break through the Lithuanian lines and was killed. By one account a lance through the neck killed him.
phases.quote: As von Jungingen attempted to break through the Lithuanian lines, he was killed.

phases.title: The leaderless Order retreats
phases.text: Surrounded and leaderless, the Order began to retreat. Part of the routed units made for their camp. The Order had by then been outnumbered by the Polish knights and the Lithuanian cavalry.
phases.quote: Surrounded and leaderless, the Teutonic Order began to retreat.

phases.title: The camp is broken
phases.text: The knights tried to make a wagon fort of the camp, but the camp followers turned against them and joined the pursuit. The defence was soon broken and the camp ravaged; by one account more knights died there than on the field.
phases.quote: However, the defense was soon broken and the camp was ravaged.
